earth_mu_km3_s2.title: NASA NTRS: Introduction to Orbits (2021)
earth_mu_km3_s2.note: sourced: standard gravitational parameter of Earth (km^3/s^2)

moon_mu_km3_s2.title: NASA/JPL Planetary Ephemerides DE440 (Park et al. 2021); NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet
moon_mu_km3_s2.note: sourced: GM = 4902.800066 km^3/s^2 from the JPL ephemeris (NSSDCA rounds it to 0.00490 x 10^6); mean radius 1737.4 km (NSSDCA)

period.title: NASA Science: Orbits and Kepler's Laws

eclipse.title: arXiv 2007.03675, App. B Eq. 38-39 (Tradespace analysis of GNSS Space Segment Architectures)
eclipse.note: cylindrical shadow; beta-angle generalisation f = acos(sqrt(h^2+2Rh)/((R+h)cos beta))/pi

solar_array_w_per_m2.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 3 Power, Table 3-1
solar_array_w_per_m2.note: derived: ~400 W/m2 triple-junction cell x 0.85 packing x 0.77 inherent degradation (SMAD Id) = 262 W/m2; cross-check OCO 900 W / 3.88 m2 = 232 W/m2 orbit average (OCO press kit)

solar_degradation_per_year.title: MIT OCW 16.851 Satellite Engineering, PS2 solution (SMAD 11.4)
solar_degradation_per_year.note: sourced: 'Gallium Arsenide degrades at 2.75% per year (worst case)'

path_efficiency.title: MIT OCW 16.851 PS2 solution; arXiv 2007.03675 Eq. 40
path_efficiency.note: sourced: Xe = 0.6, Xd = 0.8 (peak-power tracking). Psa = (Pe*Te/Xe + Pd*Td/Xd)/Td

battery_cycle_life.title: Knap et al., Energies 2020 (NASA SSRI copy), Table 6; NASA SST-SoA Table 3-6; Dalton & Balcer, ISS Li-ion battery (NTRS)
battery_cycle_life.note: estimate: curve shaped to the sourced anchors - LEO 5,500 cycles/yr for ~5 yr at 10-40% DoD (~27,500), ISS target 60,000 cycles/10 yr, Li-ion cyclability range 2,000-70,000. Interpolated in log space.

structure_fraction.title: SMAD-style mass budget (Wertz & Larson), typical structure + harness share
structure_fraction.note: estimate: structure and harness ~20-25% of dry mass for small spacecraft

bus_base_power_w.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 8 Avionics
bus_base_power_w.note: estimate: thermal control, EPS overhead, receivers and housekeeping for a microsat

bus_base_cost_musd.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 10 Integration, Launch and Deployment
bus_base_cost_musd.note: estimate: structure, integration and test of a small-satellite bus

ops_base_cost_musd_per_year.title: NASA/JPL, NASA's Mission Operations and Communications Services (D-22674, 2003)
ops_base_cost_musd_per_year.note: estimate: small mission operations team and flight software upkeep

integration_months.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 10
integration_months.note: estimate: assembly, environmental test and launch-site campaign

link_efficiency.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 9 Communications
link_efficiency.note: estimate: protocol/coding overhead and acquisition time at the start of each pass

downlink.title: OCO launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2009)
downlink.note: GB/day = Mbps x contact minutes x 60 / 8 / 1000 x link efficiency; OCO: 150 Mbit/s x 6.75 min/day

contact_gap_factor.title: OCO launch press kit
contact_gap_factor.note: estimate: passes cluster in a few consecutive orbits, so the longest gap is about twice the average gap

storage_safety_factor.title: Design practice
storage_safety_factor.note: estimate: 50% storage margin for missed passes

ground_processing_min.title: NASA FIRMS: Fire Information for Resource Management System, near real-time data
ground_processing_min.note: estimate: FIRMS delivers near-real-time active fires within about 3 hours globally and much faster from direct broadcast; 5 min for an automated check and alert once the data is on the ground
